## Two worked fixes to do together

### Paper 2 Q3 — $\sin^3\theta+\cos^3\theta$ (he got this — reinforce the method)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Method
Given $\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\tfrac12$, square: $1+2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\tfrac14\Rightarrow\sin\theta\cos\theta
=-\tfrac38$. Then
$$\sin^3\theta+\cos^3\theta=(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)(1-\sin\theta\cos\theta)=\tfrac12\Bigl(1+\tfrac38\Bigr)
=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{11}{8}=\tfrac{11}{16}.$$
The reusable idea: **a symmetric cubic factors through the sum and the product** — the same move powers many
Paper 2 identities.
:::

### Paper 2 Q11 — the two-triangle question (his signature gap)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon=false}
## What to drill
This is the **ambiguous case** dressed as a right-triangle/parameter problem — the whole of the
**[Triangle clinic](../../lessons/triangle_clinic/class_material.qmd)** (§1–§3) and its
**[assignment](../../lessons/triangle_clinic/assignment_student.qmd)**. The fixed method: identify the known
**angle**, the **adjacent** side $c$ and the **opposite** side $a$, compute the height $h=c\sin A$, and count
by comparing $a$ with $h$ and $c$ ($a<h$ none, $a=h$ one, $h<a<c$ two, $a\ge c$ one). Bring his script so we
line his "$3/4<x<3$" up against that table.
:::
